places.name: Reedy Creek Park and Nature Center
places.address: Use 2986 Rocky River Road for Reedy Creek Nature Center and Preserve. Reedy Creek Park's athletic and playground areas use separate internal approaches, so confirm which side matches your activity.
places.summary: Reedy Creek combines a large recreation park with a nature center and preserve. Visitors can use athletic fields, playgrounds and picnic areas, or explore the nature center's live native animals, exhibits, programs, biodiversity study center, and preserve trails.
places.hours: The nature preserve is open daily from sunup to sundown. The Nature Center is open Monday-Saturday 9 a.m.-5 p.m. and Sunday 1-5 p.m.; programmed recreation facilities can keep separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, preserve-trail, and nature-center access is free. Programs, shelters, fields, leagues, rentals, and organized activities may charge or require reservations.
places.parking: Use 2986 Rocky River Road for the Nature Center and preserve. For fields, playgrounds, shelters, or other recreation amenities, select the matching Reedy Creek Park lot rather than walking across the entire property.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at the Nature Center during building hours and in developed recreation areas when open. Do not rely on indoor facilities before 9 a.m., after 5 p.m., or Sunday morning.
places.accessibility: The Nature Center provides a developed public entrance and indoor exhibits, while preserve trails vary by surface and grade. Ask staff for the best current route for mobility, sensory, stroller, or restroom needs.
places.trail: Preserve trails use natural surfaces through Piedmont forest and can be muddy, rooted, or uneven. Use the official trail map and allow more time than a paved greenway walk.
places.family: Families can choose playground and field recreation or visit live native animals, exhibits, educational programs, and forest trails at the Nature Center and Preserve.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and remove waste in permitted outdoor areas. Pets are not appropriate inside the Nature Center or around live-animal exhibits; service-animal procedures may differ.
places.picnic: Developed picnic areas and shelters are available in the park. Reserve a shelter for guaranteed group use and keep food away from wildlife and indoor animal exhibits.
places.landmarks: The key destinations are Reedy Creek Nature Center, the Dr. James F. Matthews Center for Biodiversity Studies, live-animal exhibits, preserve trails, athletic areas, playgrounds, and picnic facilities.
places.closures: Nature Center hours are narrower than preserve hours. Weather, muddy trails, programs, field conditions, maintenance, and reservations can affect individual destinations without closing the entire park.

places.name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
places.address: For the North Carolina side, begin at Oconaluftee Visitor Center, 1194 Newfound Gap Road, Cherokee, NC 28719. The park spans many distant valleys and trailheads, so navigate to the exact destination rather than the park name alone.
places.summary: Great Smoky Mountains National Park protects a vast Appalachian landscape of mountain roads, trails, waterfalls, wildlife, historic buildings, campgrounds, picnic areas, and visitor centers. Oconaluftee is the most useful staffed gateway from Cherokee.
places.hours: The park is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Secondary roads, visitor centers, campgrounds, picnic areas, mills, and other facilities use seasonal schedules and can close for weather, construction, or emergencies.
places.cost: There is no entrance fee, but every vehicle parked longer than 15 minutes must display a valid parking tag unless exempt. Camping, reservations, rentals, and some programs cost separately; a parking tag does not guarantee a space.
places.parking: Choose a specific trailhead, visitor center, overlook, or historic area before driving. Parking tags are required beyond 15 minutes, popular lots often fill between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m., and NPS recommends arriving before 8 a.m. for high-demand trailheads.
places.restroom: Restrooms are concentrated at visitor centers, campgrounds, picnic areas, and major developed stops. There are no restrooms at many trailheads or remote routes, and the campgrounds do not provide showers.
places.accessibility: Oconaluftee and Sugarlands visitor centers, many major restrooms, and selected parking areas are accessible. Sugarlands Valley Nature Trail is the park's only ADA-accessible trail; the NPS also offers selected mobility-device reservations.
places.trail: Trail conditions range from short developed walks to steep, rocky, wet backcountry routes. Check distance, elevation, river crossings, weather, closures, daylight, and current alerts for the exact trail.
places.family: Family-friendly starting points include Oconaluftee Visitor Center and Mountain Farm Museum, Sugarlands, scenic drives, short nature walks, picnic areas, ranger programs, and wildlife viewing from a safe distance.
places.dogs: Pets are allowed only in campgrounds, picnic areas, along roads, and on the Gatlinburg and Oconaluftee River trails, and must be leashed. Pets are prohibited on nearly all other trails; never leave them unattended.
places.picnic: The park has ten developed picnic areas with tables, grills, and varying seasonal schedules. Some pavilions are reservable; remove all food and trash because bears and other wildlife are active.
places.landmarks: North Carolina highlights include Oconaluftee, Mountain Farm Museum, Mingus Mill, Newfound Gap, Kuwohi, Deep Creek, Cataloochee, Smokemont, waterfalls, historic structures, and extensive mountain trails.
places.closures: Weather, flooding, wildfire, bear activity, construction, rockfall, and winter conditions can close roads or trails quickly. Check NPS alerts and road status immediately before entering; the park can remain open while your destination is inaccessible.

places.name: Romare Bearden Park
places.address: Use 300 S. Church Street, Charlotte, NC 28202. The park fills the block beside Truist Field between Church, Mint, Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, and Third Street.
places.summary: Romare Bearden Park is a 5.4-acre Uptown destination inspired by artist Romare Bearden's collages, with skyline views, event lawn, gardens, waterfalls and water features, dining courtyard, interactive chimes, public art, seating, and year-round programs.
places.hours: Use is governed by posted Mecklenburg County park hours and event restrictions; the County does not currently surface a dependable park-specific daily schedule in its new facility directory. Confirm before a late-night or event-dependent visit.
places.cost: Ordinary park access is free. Nearby parking, concessions, reserved events, commercial activity, and ticketed programs may cost separately.
places.parking: There is no dedicated free visitor lot. Use a signed Uptown garage, paid surface lot, legal street space, transit, or walking route; Truist Field games and stadium events sharply increase demand and prices.
places.restroom: Do not assume a dedicated public restroom is continuously available in the park. Plan around nearby staffed venues or event facilities and confirm access before bringing children or anyone with urgent restroom needs.
places.accessibility: The compact downtown park has paved perimeter walks and developed plazas, but lawns, crushed-granite areas, crowds, water features, and event barriers can alter routes. Approach from the side closest to your destination.
places.trail: This is a compact urban walking and gathering park rather than a trail destination. Paved downtown sidewalks connect it with Truist Field, transit, museums, stadiums, and nearby Uptown blocks.
places.family: Children often enjoy the open lawn, waterfalls, water features, interactive digital and dance chimes, gardens, skyline views, and programmed events. Closely supervise around water and crowded game-day streets.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed, remove waste, and obey posted event or turf restrictions. Dense crowds, loud events, water features, and hot pavement can make some visits unsuitable for pets.
places.picnic: Tables, chairs, lawn, gardens, and nearby takeout support casual meals. Organized gatherings, equipment, vendors, alcohol, or exclusive areas can require County approval.
places.landmarks: Signature elements include the Charlotte skyline view, Truist Field backdrop, Spiral Odyssey sculpture, event green, waterfalls, gardens, dining courtyard, and interactive chimes inspired by Romare Bearden's art.
places.closures: Concerts, festivals, private reservations, security incidents, turf recovery, maintenance, severe weather, and nearby stadium events can restrict lawns, water features, streets, or the full park.
